editorial:
You follow two New Orleans paramedics as their normal shifts turn into a nightmare when a new street drug starts causing impossible deaths. One man is facing a deadly illness, while the other is worried about his missing daughter. The movie mixes emergency-room tension with strange time jumps, so you get both human drama and sci-fi mystery. It feels grounded at first, then slowly pulls you into a darker, stranger world where every choice matters.

The acting keeps you invested, especially in the friendship and family stress, and the time-travel rules are easy to follow without feeling confusing. The pacing is steady, though some scenes feel heavy and the ending may not answer every question you have. If you like smart thrillers with a sad edge, this is a good pick.
endingExplained: Steve learns the drug sends users back in time for seven minutes, and his brain tumor makes him able to survive the trips. After Brianna disappears, he buys the remaining supply and tests the rules. He travels to the past, finds her trapped there, and gives her the last pill so she can return home. Steve stays behind, choosing to save her instead of himself, while Dennis and Brianna reunite in the present.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves time-travel thrillers with emotional stakes.
